title: The 1 p.m. shift that came first

public.summary: A function that finds the earliest shift sometimes picks an afternoon shift. Find the cause and choose a fix.
public.statement: A food-bank rota stores shift start times as text on a 24-hour clock, such as "9:30" or "13:00". earliestShift() should return the shift with the earliest start time. With shifts starting at "9:30" and "13:00", it returns the 13:00 shift. Identify the faulty line and choose a change that makes the function correct for any valid times.
facts: Times look like "H:MM" or "HH:MM"; hours may have one or two digits.
shifts always contains at least one shift.

lines: const toMinutes = (t) => { const [h, m] = t.split(":").map(Number); return h * 60 + m; };

constraints.text: Return the shift whose start time is earliest in the day.
Must work when one-digit and two-digit hours are mixed (e.g. "9:30" and "13:00").

answer_format.instructions: Choose the faulty line and the fix.

fields.label: Which line makes the wrong choice?
Which change makes the function correct?

public.explanation_prompt: Why does "13:00" look earlier than "9:30" to the original code? What inputs did you use to check your fix?

provenance.author: Reasoning Lab project team
provenance.contamination_note: String comparison of times is a known bug pattern; option c is a less obvious but valid alternative.

reviewed_explanation.text: Line 6 compares the times as text, character by character, so "13:00" < "9:30" is true because "1" comes before "9". Converting both to minutes (option a) fixes it. Padding both to five characters with leading zeros (option c) also works, because "09:30" and "13:00" then compare correctly as text. Comparing lengths (option b) ignores the actual time, and Number("9:30") is NaN (option d), so every comparison is false.
reviewed_explanation.accepted_summary: Line 6 with fix a or fix c.

review.notes: Patch outcomes confirmed by running reviewed cases.
